name: BigQuery Standard SQL
title: BigQuery Standard SQL (2026)

type.text: **No sum types**: an alternative is a nullable column, a STRUCT field checked by convention, or a JSON half-type, and the consumer re-derives the encoding
**No generic parameter**: queries are typed per statement, and a routine over "any table" needs dynamic SQL or a fixed signature
**NULL is a member of every domain**: columns, parameters, and scripting variables carry NULL unannounced, three-valued logic decides comparisons, and no signature records the guard
**Statements state no effect**: an INSERT in a script, a CREATE in a loop, and an EXPORT look alike in the signature, and nothing tracks what a statement touches
**JavaScript rides the boundary**: SQL UDFs can be defined in JavaScript inside the query, and values cross between GoogleSQL types and the JS runtime with no checked boundary

construction.text: **The query is the program**: WITH, scripting blocks, and table functions compose declaratively, and the same text replays against any authorized dataset
**Tables mutate in place**: DML rewrites in place with no immutability construct, and time travel is the engine's retention feature rather than a language construct

memory.text: **Allocation is the service's**: slots, spill, and shuffle live in Google's fleet, and the query text allocates nothing

error.text: **The handler decides, or the script dies**: BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR wraps a statement block, and without it the failed statement ends the script — no value carries the failure
**No composable result type**: failures travel by exception and results by tables, arrays, and scalar variables, and neither threads through an expression

concurrency.text: **Session state is shared**: session variables and temporary tables are visible across every statement and routine the session runs

platform.text: **The query runs only in BigQuery**: GoogleSQL's functions, scripting, and authorization model are the service's, and nothing in the language runs without it
**A poor fit outside analytical work**: the language has no general libraries or error values, and transactional application logic is explicitly the wrong shape for the engine

performance.text: **The service states its own cost**: query execution details break a query into per-stage timings and row counts, and INFORMATION_SCHEMA publishes the job's plan
**The bytes are the bill**: on-demand pricing charges scanned bytes, so a SELECT's column list is a cost decision the syntax barely surfaces

ecosystem.text: **A proprietary service end to end**: the engine, storage, and authorization are Google Cloud products under commercial terms, with no self-hostable reference
**Two dialects ride along**: legacy SQL remains documented beside Standard SQL for old jobs, and the migration between them is a burden new work still meets

evolution.text: **The service moves under the queries**: release notes document deprecations and behavior changes on a continuous cadence, and SQL text that ran last quarter can shift under a scheduled job

domain.text: **Adopting GoogleSQL means adopting BigQuery**: datasets, authorized views, slots, and the storage model define what a query can say, and the same vocabulary is the deployment

**The cost and partitioning model dictates the schema**: partitioned and clustered tables, denormalized nesting, and bytes-scanned pricing drive table design — the published guidance makes the data model follow what the engine bills

learning.text: **SQL plus a scripting layer plus UDFs**: GoogleSQL carries statements, procedural blocks, SQL and JavaScript routines, and TVFs, and the surface exceeds the SQL a new reader already knows

syntax.text: **Standard-shaped, Google-flavored**: the core reads like ANSI SQL, and arrays, STRUCTs, scripting, and the qualifier grammar are the dialect's own layer

testing.text: **No standard test harness for queries**: the documented testing story is dbt and third-party frameworks against a billed project, and the language names no regression harness

security.text: **Dynamic SQL is string-built**: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE runs text assembled at run time in scripts, so concatenated user input reaches the parser, and the documented mitigation is parameterized queries and query parameters

reproducibility.text: **A query is request text**: the same GoogleSQL on the same data and service state reproduces the same answer, and nothing is built
**The executing engine is unpinnable**: the repository names no engine build — the service's continuous releases decide semantics, and no file can record them

supplychain.text: **No signed provenance for published queries or routines**: shared datasets, saved queries, and routines move through the service under IAM terms, with no signature-checked distribution channel
**No advisory feed names the query surface**: changes and fixes land in release notes, with no CVE-mapped advisory database for the engine's dependencies

observability.text: **No tracing standard is part of the language**: Cloud Monitoring and audit logs are platform features, and the query text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: jobs log to the service, and no logging construct exists in GoogleSQL

feedback.text: **The vendor's IDE completes the query**: BigQuery Studio publishes SQL editing with autocompletion and run control as part of the service
**No debugger exists for scripts**: diagnosis goes through execution details, job information, and error messages

interop.text: **No portable target**: the query runs on BigQuery, and nothing in the language runs without the service

governance.text: **Governance is Google**: the dialect's direction and cadence are one company's, and no independent body can change them
**No public specification exists**: the GoogleSQL reference documents the implemented behavior of one service, and no independent implementation follows from it
**Correctness is what the service does**: no conformance suite exists for GoogleSQL, and the one implementation is the oracle

tradeoffs: **The bill is part of the language**: bytes-scanned pricing makes column pruning and partitioning design decisions, and the price is a data model shaped by the meter
**Serverless scale without a server**: slots and shuffle absorb the workload, and the price is a runtime whose version, limits, and behavior are the service's, never the repository's
**Scripting turns SQL into a program**: variables, loops, transactions, and EXCEPTION blocks deploy real logic, and the price is logic with no debugger, no result type, and no test harness
**JavaScript UDFs buy portability of logic**: a function body moves to the query, and the price is an unchecked boundary between two type systems inside one statement
verdict: BigQuery Standard SQL is GoogleSQL — analytical SQL with arrays and STRUCTs, a scripting layer with procedures, transactions, and EXCEPTION blocks, SQL and JavaScript UDFs, and table functions — served by one proprietary engine. Its costs are the service's own: NULL in every domain, failures that travel only by exception, session-wide state, bytes-scanned pricing that shapes the data model, and continuous engine releases no repository can pin. Main strengths: per-stage execution details inside the service, vendor IDE tooling, a declarative core that composes cleanly, and one reference that states the whole surface. Main weaknesses: no specification or conformance mechanism, single-vendor governance, a proprietary stack with no self-hostable reference, no debugger or standard test harness, string-built dynamic SQL, and a legacy-SQL burden the docs still carry.

energy.text: Energy is Google's fleet and the project's bill: slots, storage, and scanned bytes pay, and the reader's levers are partitioning and column design the query text exposes but does not control.

ai-readiness.text: BigQuery ships agent-facing data surfaces (data canvas, Gemini-assisted SQL), and SQL is the model-trained lingua franca — generated queries still meet the traps: three-valued logic, bytes-scanned cost, and scripting scope.

safety.text: No certified path; the service's durability, IAM, and audit guarantees are Google's, stated in its own documentation and terms.

use:data.observation: datasets, authorized views, slots, and the storage model define what a query can say

use:query.observation: the core reads like ANSI SQL

delivery.note: queries travel as GoogleSQL text to the service, which parses and executes them; routines and scripts are stored by the service as source; no compiled unit crosses a boundary
